data.narrative:
Quantum Motion is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $160M+ to date. The broader quantum computing sector comprises 11 comparable entities—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private (including Quantinuum, IonQ pre-IPO, Rigetti pre-IPO, Infleqtion, and others)—providing context for frontier-tech valuation practices in this domain.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing cohort; applying an all-sector median would risk misrepresenting Quantum Motion's risk and growth profile. Stage-progression analysis was therefore the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised ($160M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression to the next institutional milestone yields $272M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $231M to $313M, centered on $272M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity around the single-method estimate, acknowledging the data constraints. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier for quantum computing specifically (versus general venture stage progression), the absence of transaction comps at identical stage and sector intersection, and the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of the quantum hardware sector, which may diverge from traditional venture patterns. A fuller valuation would benefit from direct revenue or burn-rate metrics and institutional round terms.
